minor_characters.name: The Director of Companies (captain of the Nellie)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Frame narrator’s host on the Thames in Ch 001 and the voice that ends the frame in Ch 003.
minor_characters.reason_removable: The frame only requires anonymous listeners aboard the Nellie, so his titled presence can be merged into an unnamed ‘captain/listener’ without affecting plot or themes.

minor_characters.name: The Lawyer (aboard the Nellie)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: One of Marlow’s silent listeners on the yacht in Ch 001.
minor_characters.reason_removable: He contributes no action or unique perspective beyond being one of the generic listeners required by the frame.

minor_characters.name: The Accountant (aboard the Nellie, frame character)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Another of the silent listeners in Ch 001 (not the Company accountant at the Outer Station).
minor_characters.reason_removable: He is redundant as an individual since the synopsis only needs an audience on the Nellie, not this titled listener.

minor_characters.name: The compassionate secretary (Brussels)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Briefly ushers Marlow through contract formalities in Ch 001.
minor_characters.reason_removable: The synopsis already covers Marlow’s hiring in Brussels, so this clerk’s sympathetic color can be dropped.

minor_characters.name: The shabby clerk escort (Brussels)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Takes Marlow to the doctor and trades small talk over a drink in Ch 001.
minor_characters.reason_removable: He adds only incidental local color to the Brussels sequence and can be omitted without loss.

minor_characters.name: The Company ‘great man’ in Brussels
minor_characters.appearances_summary: A brief handshake meeting with the local Company head in Ch 001.
minor_characters.reason_removable: Marlow’s appointment is already secured by his aunt’s influence, so this faceless executive is nonessential.

minor_characters.name: The Swede (coastal steamer captain)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Ferries Marlow up the coast and mentions a suicide in Ch 001.
minor_characters.reason_removable: He is a one-scene ferry for transport logistics and can be elided while Marlow simply ‘proceeds inland.’

minor_characters.name: The manager’s uncle (leader of the Eldorado Expedition)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Appears in Ch 001–002 hovering around the Central Station and whispering with the manager before vanishing upriver.
minor_characters.reason_removable: The synopsis requires the Eldorado Expedition to appear, not the uncle’s person or private chats, so he can be dropped while keeping the expedition as a group.

minor_characters.name: Van Shuyten (Dutch trader on the coast, mentioned by the Russian)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Named in Ch 002 as the Russian’s outfitter before the interior wanderings.
minor_characters.reason_removable: He exists only in the Russian’s backstory and has no effect on events or themes.

minor_characters.name: Mr. Towson/Towser (author of the seamanship manual)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Named on the title page of the found book at the reed hut in Ch 002.
minor_characters.reason_removable: The synopsis needs the manual as a talisman of reality, not its author’s name.

minor_characters.name: The Company agent with gold-rimmed spectacles (Europe)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Calls on Marlow after his return in Ch 003 to demand Kurtz’s papers for the Company.
minor_characters.reason_removable: The synopsis only requires that Marlow refuses the Company’s attempts to seize the papers, which can be narrated without this specific emissary.

subplots.name: The manager and his uncle’s whispered schemes against Kurtz
subplots.reason_removable: Their balcony-of-the-bush conniving is duplicative of the manager’s envy and bad faith already shown elsewhere and has no bearing on the river journey’s outcomes.

subplots.name: The boilermaker’s pigeon-fancying friendship with Marlow
subplots.reason_removable: It is charming color around the ‘rivets’ obsession but does not alter the repair, departure, or any later consequence.

subplots.name: Marlow’s fainting white companion and the wrecked hammock episode on the overland trek
subplots.reason_removable: This side adventure only underscores the general futility and can be cut without changing the passage to the Central Station or Marlow’s arc.

subplots.name: The Eldorado Expedition’s later fate (the dead donkeys)
subplots.reason_removable: Reporting their eventual ruin adds satiric closure but has no effect on Marlow’s repair, voyage, or meeting with Kurtz.

subplots.name: The Russian trader’s personal backstory (runaway schoolboy, English ships, arch-priest father, outfitted by Van Shuyten)
subplots.reason_removable: Only his present role—devoted go-between for Kurtz and source of key revelations—matters to the plot.

digressions.topic: Long historical catalogue of the Thames’ heroic past (Drake to Franklin; Golden Hind to Erebus and Terror)
digressions.reason_removable: This soaring prelude can be compressed to ‘the Thames has launched conquests’ without harming the frame or throughline.

digressions.topic: Coastal voyage vignettes, including the French man-of-war ‘firing into a continent’ and catacomb-like ports
digressions.reason_removable: These set tone but do not set up any later action or character turn beyond what briefer summary can supply.

digressions.topic: Technical layout of the steamboat and pilot-house furnishings
digressions.reason_removable: The inventory of couch, shutters, gauges, rifles, and wheel adds mechanics but no stakes or meaning not conveyed elsewhere.

digressions.topic: Economic aside on cannibals’ brass-wire ‘pay’ and rotten hippo-meat provisions
digressions.reason_removable: The micro-economy details can be tightened to a line about hunger and restraint without loss of the theme or plot.

digressions.topic: Mini-essay praising Towson’s seamanship manual as ‘unmistakably real’
digressions.reason_removable: The manual must be found, but its page-long eulogy can be pared down to a sentence and still serve as Marlow’s tether to reality.
